model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity on tangible book (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E total revenue (NII + noninterest income) EX-NOTABLES, built from 9M-2026 actuals (total revenue 7,198.1 less the $540.1M Visa second-exchange-offer gain, less the $34.0M guardianship sale gain, plus the $73.9M AFS repositioning loss = 6,697.9 underlying, +12.3% on 9M-2025's 5,963.3) plus Q4-2026 at ~2,250 (+6% on Q4-2025's 2,123.1, the middle of management's mid-single-digit-to-~7% Q4 guide) = 8,948, rounded to 8,950 (+10.7% on FY2025's 8,086.4). Prior version (2026-10-02) used 8,880 from H1 actuals and the July +9-10% guide. Same FY0-run-rate convention as NAB.AX.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 181,117,806 common shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover page and balance sheet) plus 1.14M dilutive share-based awards (Q3-2026 diluted 183,173,621 less basic 182,037,839 weighted average) = 182.3M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed inside noninterest expense; buybacks (FY2025 $1,273.5M, 9M-2026 $1,061.8M) are the distribution mechanism for FCFE, not a modelled count reduction.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank convention (house precedent NAB.AX, HBAN, GL): deposits ($132.2B at 2026-09-30), other borrowings and senior/subordinated notes are operating funding of a deposit-taker and are already serviced inside net interest income; FCFE is post-interest, so net debt is held at 0 and the flows are capitalised at the cost of equity. The only claim senior to common deducted is the $884.9M of preferred stock (Series D $493.5M + Series E $391.4M carrying value) in equity_bridge.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is the FY2026E FCFE proxy: net income ex-notables 2,172 (pretax 2,915 at a 32.6% margin, 25.5% tax) less 766 of capital retention at 0.8 x the 10.7% FY2026 revenue growth. It is lower than the prior version's 1,421 only because faster FY0 growth raises the formula retention; the engine does not read it (the flows are built from base_revenue and the driver paths). reported_fcf is the CSV's FY2025 OCF-less-capex (5,459.5) and is deposit-flow noise for a bank (FY2024 was -587.5; 9M-2026 OCF 1,440); it is recorded for auditability only and the owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does NOT hold on this route.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense FY2025 = $126.5M (1.56% of revenue); no separate equity-award tax figure published - net-share-settlement withholding (450k shares FY2025) is treated as part of the buyback cash. SBC is already inside noninterest expense, so the pretax margin is post-SBC; sbc_pct_path is carried explicitly so the engine's house/street band is computed.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the business for a bank (NII 2,411 FY2025). Nothing is added back as net cash, so there is no double count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $1,273.5M plus common dividends $591.6M = $1,865M returned vs $1,695M net income to common (110% payout). 9M-2026: treasury stock purchased $1,061.8M + common dividends declared $461.5M = $1,523M vs $1,923.5M net income to common (79% of GAAP earnings, ~97% of earnings ex the after-tax Visa gain). Quarterly dividend raised 10% to $0.88 in Q3-2026 ($3.52 annualised).
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the FY2026 ex-notables estimate (fiscal year closes 31 Dec 2026; nine months reported, Q4 guided), so Y1 = FY2027. Last fully reported year is FY2025.

balance_sheet_anchors.cet1_ratio_note: CET1 12.4% standardized / 14.4% advanced at 2026-09-30 (12.6% / 15.0% at YE2025; ~12.0% at Q1-2026); CET1 capital $11,555.6M; stress capital buffer 2.5% and 7.0% CET1 minimum held until 2027-10-01
balance_sheet_anchors.note: Preferred is the balance-sheet carrying value of Series D ($493.5M, 5,000 shares) plus Series E ($391.4M, 16,000 shares). CORRECTION to the prior version, which described the whole $885M as 'Series E at 4.70%' backed out of the dividend: the total was right, the label was not. Period-end deposits fell 7.4% from YE2025 and 9.2% from 2026-06-30 ($145.6B); average deposits fell ~3.5% sequentially in Q3. AOCI loss widened from -551.7 (Q2) to -718.7; as a Category II institution NTRS deducts AFS unrealised losses from regulatory capital.

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 9.75% in USD: 10-yr UST ~4.25%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.1 for a custody/trust bank (higher operating leverage to market levels and rates than a retail bank, no credit-cycle balance sheet to speak of). Single rate across all three scenarios so risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates. Labelled 'wacc' only because that is the engine's field name; no debt is in the capital structure being discounted.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (premises) are expensed inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the pretax margin; no lease liability is added to net debt and no separate lease line is carried (treatment A, applied once).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; net income is fully attributable to the parent.
inputs.engine_mapping: The component engine is driven as a bank P&L: 'EBITDA margin' = pretax-income margin + D&A % + SBC %, so that EBITDA - SBC - D&A = pretax income; cash_tax_rate 25.5% (FY2025 effective 25.8%, H1-2026 25.4%) turns that into net income; da_pct and capex_pct share an 8.8% core (FY2025 depreciation/amortisation/accretion 779.1 vs software 700.2 + premises 74.0 = 774.2 of capex, i.e. D&A ~= capex), and the EXCESS of capex_pct over da_pct is the capital retained to fund balance-sheet growth at a ~12% CET1 - retention = k x revenue growth, with k = 0.8 base / 0.7 bull / 1.3 bear (TCE/revenue is ~1.32x, so k = 1.3 assumes RWA grows one-for-one with revenue; 0.8 reflects that roughly half of NTRS's growth is ad-valorem fee growth on AUC/A that consumes no RWA - over FY2019-25 tangible common grew ~1.5%/yr against ~4%/yr underlying revenue growth with a ~95% average payout). Working-capital capture is 0. The resulting flow is FCFE = net income - retained capital, capitalised at the cost of equity, and the Series D and E preferred is deducted in the bridge instead of its $41.8M dividend being deducted from the flows (par deduction is the more conservative of the two at a 9.75% cost of equity).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE at cost of equity, through the component engine route - unchanged from the 2026-10-02 valuation (routing table's bank row implemented as the house precedent for HBAN, NAB.AX and GL does it: net_debt = 0, preferred deducted in equity_bridge, retention tied to growth). BVPS-compounding rejected because NTRS distributes ~100% of earnings; owner-FCF DCF rejected because OCF swings with deposit flows (-486 FY2024, +5,534 FY2025). SBC expensed inside noninterest expense, share count held flat. UPDATE 2026-11-19 (Q3-2026 10-Q, results 2026-10-21): anchors refreshed to the 2026-09-30 balance sheet (182.3M diluted shares, $884.9M preferred), FY0 revenue lifted 8,880 -> 8,950 on nine-month actuals and the Q4 guide. FY0 ANCHOR: revenue 8,950, pretax margin 32.6%, net income ex-notables 2,172, EPS ex-notables ~$11.7 after preferred dividends - 14.7x at the current price. 9M-2026 underlying pretax = 2,561.8 reported - 540.1 Visa - 34.0 guardianship + 73.9 AFS loss + 145.6 notable expenses = 2,207.2 (33.0% of 6,697.9); Q3 alone 33.3%; Q4 assumed ~2,250 revenue / ~1,540 expense (31.6%), giving full-year expense growth ex-notables of ~4.9% against revenue +10.7%, i.e. ~580bps of operating leverage, consistent with the raised '>500bps' guide. CORRECTION: the prior version described Q2-2026 notable expenses as '~$220M restructuring' and an H1 underlying pretax margin of 34.5%. The 10-Q itemises $145.6M (software dispositions 61.5, severance 51.0, Invested-as-One equity grant 33.1), which puts the H1 underlying margin at 32.8%. This did not flow into any driver (FY0's margin is not an engine input and the forward margin paths are absolute levels), so it changes no value, but the prior headroom between H1 and the 32.0% FY0 margin was overstated. DRIVERS CHANGED: base FY2027 only (growth 4.0 -> 3.5, pretax margin 31.5 -> 32.0, retention follows growth) and bear FY2027-28 (growth -2.0 -> -3.0; CET1 rebuild add 1.5% -> 0.5% of revenue). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: every base and bear path from FY2028 (bear FY2029) onward, the whole bull case, k (0.8/0.7/1.3), the 25.5% tax rate, the 9.75% cost of equity, terminal growth and caps, and the 25/50/25 weights - see unchanged_assumptions. Tax: 9M-2026 effective rate was 23.5% (Q3 19.3%) on a reduction in the valuation allowance for US foreign tax credits; treated as non-recurring, 25.5% held. DATA FLAG for the parent (still open): the CSV's interim 'Revenue' rows (Q3-2026 1,373.0, Q2 1,349.5, Q1 1,341.4) are the ASC-606 trust-fee subset, not total revenue (true Q3-2026 = 2,294.4) - the HBAN tag-preference trap; FY rows are correct totals. The KPI NetInterestIncome Q3-2026 671.4 is GAAP (679.1 FTE).

equity_bridge.item: Series D and Series E noncumulative perpetual preferred stock (carrying value)
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet: Series D $493.5M + Series E $391.4M. Senior to common; deducted in full rather than charging the $41.8M/yr preferred dividend to the flows (the more conservative of the two at a 9.75% cost of equity).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2027-FY2031 average revenue growth (4.0-5.0%); equity CAGR rejected as the anchor because NTRS pays out ~100% of earnings (110% in FY2025), which mechanically suppresses book growth without saying anything about earnings power
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 2.1% vs revenue 5.8% and EPS 9.9% - divergence >30%. Cause is distribution policy (buybacks shrank the diluted count from 208.3M to 192.2M over FY2020-25 and AOCI moved from positive to -590.5M), not a deteriorating franchise. EPS CAGRs are flattered at the 3-yr point by FY2022's low base (6.16) and by buybacks; revenue CAGRs are clean of the FY2024 Visa gain because FY2025 is the end point.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are computed on NET INCOME (the FCFE proxy: FY2025 1,736.9 vs FY2022 1,336.0 vs FY2020 1,209.3), not on the CSV's reported FCF, which is deposit-flow noise for a bank (FY2024 -587.5, FY2025 +5,459.5). Revenue: FY2025 8,086.4 / FY2022 6,761.2 / FY2020 6,100.8. EPS: 8.78 / 6.16 / 5.48. Equity: 12,957.9 / 11,259.5 / 11,688.3. All FY-end December.

base.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin = EBITDA - SBC - D&A = [32.0, 32.0, 32.5, 33.0, 33.0, ...]. FY2027 gives back ~60bps from FY0's 32.6% as capital-markets/securities-lending revenue and deposit-funded NII normalise (prior version: 31.5% against a 32.0% FY0; lifted 50bps because nine months at 33.0% and the raised >500bps operating-leverage guide show more of the 2026 cost discipline is in the run-rate). FY2028 onward is the prior path, untouched: 33% by FY2030, NTRS's own FY2018-19 level.
base.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.8 x revenue growth = [2.8, 4.0, 4.0, 3.6, 3.6, 3.2, 3.2, 2.8, 2.4, 2.4]% of revenue; terminal retention 2.4% of revenue is ~10% of net income, i.e. a ~90% payout at 3% growth, matching NTRS's FY2019-25 average.
base.terminal_note: Cap 15x FCFE (~13x net income) is the exit a buyer of a mature trust bank plausibly pays (NTRS 10-yr forward P/E range ~11-17x); Gordon at 9.75%/3.0% is 15.3x so the cap binds marginally.
base.growth_note: FY2027 growth trimmed 4.0 -> 3.5: FY0 is now 0.8% higher on capital-markets and NII strength that management itself says may not fully persist, period-end deposits are down 7.4% since year-end (average -3.5% QoQ in Q3) and the Q4 NII guide (+8-9% YoY) is already a deceleration from Q3's +14%. Net effect: FY2027 revenue 9,263 vs 9,235 in the prior version. FY2028+ unchanged.

bull.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [33.0, 33.5, 34.0, 34.5, 35.0, 35.0, ...]: the 2026 operating-leverage run-rate is sustained (restructuring savings land, trust-fee growth stays high-single-digit), reaching a BNY-like 35% pretax margin.
bull.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.7 x revenue growth: more of the growth is capital-light fee growth (alternatives servicing, family-office wealth), so less CET1 is consumed per dollar of revenue.

bear.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [28.5, 28.0, 28.5, 29.0, 29.5, 30.0, ...] - unchanged. FY2027 revenue falls 3% (capital markets/securities lending -25% from the 2026 peak, NIM compression as the Fed eases, deposit run-off continuing from the Q3-2026 decline, flat market levels) while the cost base is sticky, so the margin drops to FY2023's ~28% and recovers only to 30%.
bear.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 1.3 x revenue growth (RWA grows one-for-one with revenue; floored at zero in the FY2027 shrink year, so no capital release is credited) plus 0.5% of revenue in FY2027-28 (~$45M/yr) of CET1 rebuild. The add was 1.5% in the prior version against a Basel III endgame RWA uplift of 5-15%; the March 2026 reproposal removes that case (NTRS's own preliminary estimate in the Q3 10-Q is a modest DECREASE in RWA), so the residual 0.5% now covers AOCI drag (AFS losses are deducted from capital for a Category II bank; AOCI widened to -718.7) and final-rule uncertainty. Terminal cap 13x FCFE reflects a de-rated, slower-growing trust bank.
bear.growth_note: FY2027 -2.0 -> -3.0 so the bear's absolute FY2027 revenue (8,682) is not mechanically lifted by the higher FY0 (prior 8,702), and to carry the new deposit-run-off risk. FY2028+ unchanged.

scenario_narratives.base: Northern Trust's value turns on three axes: (1) organic trust-fee growth on AUC/A of $19.8T and AUM of $1.96T (+11% YoY), which the base case holds at mid-single digits as market levels compound and alternatives/family-office mandates add net new business; (2) net interest income, ~28% of revenue, which gives back some of 2026's expansion (NIM 1.83% in Q3-26, NII +14% YoY) as the Fed eases and as the deposit base - down 7.4% at period end since December, with average deposits off ~3.5% in Q3 alone - proves less sticky than the 2026 run-rate assumes, netting revenue growth to 3.5% in FY2027, 4-5% through FY2031 and 3% thereafter; (3) operating leverage, where nine months at a 33.0% underlying pretax margin and a full-year guide raised to >500bps put FY0 at 32.6%; FY2027 is modelled as a soft year (60bps give-back to 32.0%) before the margin climbs to 33% - the level NTRS already achieved in FY2018-19 - rather than to BNY's mid-30s. Capital retention runs at 0.8x growth, so ~90% of earnings is distributed through the dividend (raised to $0.88 quarterly) and buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: Unchanged from the prior version. Fee growth stays high-single-digit as the alternatives-servicing and ultra-high-net-worth franchises take share and equity markets keep compounding; capital-markets and securities-lending income holds near the 2026 level instead of mean-reverting; deposits stabilise; the restructuring charges convert into durable cost savings so the 2026 operating-leverage run-rate persists and the pretax margin reaches 35% by FY2031. Lower capital intensity (0.7x growth), a stable 12%+ CET1 and a Basel III endgame that modestly reduces RWA let payout stay ~100%. Q3-2026 is consistent with this path (FY2027 at 33.0% is only 40bps above FY0) but one more quarter of it is not evidence about FY2028-31, so the path is not raised. The scarcity value of being one of three scaled global custodians (BNY Mellon's 2025 approach) is NOT separately priced.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2027 air-pocket materialises: capital-markets and securities-lending revenue falls a quarter from cyclically high levels, Fed easing compresses NIM while the deposit run-off that began in Q3-2026 continues, and flat equity markets stall ad-valorem fee growth, so revenue drops 3% against a sticky cost base and the pretax margin falls to FY2023's ~28%. Basel III endgame is no longer the capital shock it was in the prior version (the March 2026 reproposal lifts the strictest-standard threshold to $700B and NTRS estimates a modest RWA decrease), so the extra retention is cut to ~$45M/yr for two years of AOCI-driven CET1 repair; the sub-scale franchise then grows only 2.5-3% with the margin recovering to 30%, and the market exits at 13x FCFE. No solvency or going-concern element - a de-rating and an earnings reset, not a credit event.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Held at 25/50/25 (house default 15/50/35), deliberately. Two things moved since October and they offset: the Basel III endgame overhang that helped justify a 25% bear has eased (reproposal, CET1 back to 12.4%), but the bear's core mechanism - NII and capital-markets income normalising in 2027 - has gained a new, concrete data point in the deposit decline, and interest-rate sensitivity remains the Analysis's only high-severity risk. Bull stays at 25% because it still needs sustained peak capital-markets income, durable cost savings and benign rates together, and consensus remains Hold with targets in the $180s. What would move the weights: deposits stabilising or regrowing through Q4-26/Q1-27 with NIM held near 1.8% would argue for 20/50/30; a second sequential average-deposit decline of similar size, or a 2027 NII guide below flat, would argue for 30/50/20.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Northern Trust is a fee-led trust and custody bank that distributes essentially all of its earnings, so it is valued as a stream of free cash flow to equity (net income less the capital retained to grow risk-weighted assets at a ~12% CET1) capitalised at a 9.75% USD cost of equity, with deposits and wholesale funding treated as operating liabilities and only the $884.9M of preferred deducted ahead of common. FY0 is the FY2026 guided run-rate with the Visa and guardianship gains, the securities loss and the software/severance/equity-grant charges stripped out, so the valuation does not capitalise a one-off. The three cases differ on where capital-markets income settles after 2026, how much of the 2026 operating leverage is structural, and how much capital Basel III endgame absorbs.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net interest income (~28% of revenue) is the swing factor: a faster or deeper Fed easing cycle than guidance assumes compresses NIM from the 1.83% Q3-26 level and takes FY2027 revenue growth negative, as in the bear case

NEW - deposit durability: period-end deposits fell to $132.2B from $142.8B at YE2025 and $145.6B at Q2-26 (average deposits -3.5% QoQ in Q3). 2026's NII growth rests on that base; continued run-off is the most direct route from the base case to the bear case
2026 capital-markets, FX and securities-lending income is cyclically elevated (+69% YoY in Q2); the base case already assumes moderation, but a sharp reversal produces the FY2027 air-pocket
Ad-valorem trust fees make ~55% of revenue directly sensitive to equity and bond market levels; a 20% market drawdown would cut fee revenue high-single-digits with a lag

Basel III endgame is a reduced risk: the March 2026 reproposal lifts the strictest-standard threshold to $700B and NTRS's preliminary estimate is a modest RWA decrease, but the rule is not final; the bear case keeps a small two-year CET1 rebuild and 1.3x-growth retention

2026 notable charges ($145.6M of software dispositions, severance and one-time equity grants in Q2) must convert into durable cost savings; if the efficiency programme stalls, the base case's 33% pretax margin is not reached

The model holds the share count flat and treats buybacks as the FCFE distribution channel; the per-share value is therefore insensitive to the pace of repurchases but sensitive to the 25.5% tax rate and 9.75% cost of equity (see sensitivity grid)
